- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment spikes) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices during strong negative sentiment — increase forecast lows to avoid under-shooting.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes — cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below true peak or adjust downward by 0.5–1.5 standard deviations.
- Mean-revert forecasts when sentiment is consistently negative — avoid prolonged upward bias.
- Lagged forecast errors are common — adjust for 1–3 day delay in price reaction to sentiment shifts.
- For 30-day horizon, reduce forecast volatility when sentiment is stable or trending flat — avoid over-optimistic swings.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a dip, forecast should not overshoot — cap upward momentum at 10–15% above recent high.
